description: pyGSFLOW is a Python package for building, reading, editing and examining GSFLOW hydrological models. The developer repository documents support for GSFLOW and PRMS, together with MODFLOW functions exposed through FloPy. It brings model-file preparation and output visualisation into a scripted workflow and supplies tutorial examples. A modeller can use it to construct surface-water and groundwater simulations for water-supply or irrigation questions. Application extent, grid and time step remain properties of the model inputs, not a fixed global dataset. The source is free on GitHub under the Unlicense, and the README links official USGS releases. A limitation is that the documented supplied GSFLOW executables target Windows and Linux; the README does not offer a compiled macOS version. FloPy and the underlying solvers remain required dependencies. No directly related catalogue record was established. This review inspected documentation and metadata without installing executables or checking model calibration.
